name: Connected Local Agreement Graphs
statement: Fix $1\le r<N$ and choose one binary pattern $f_T$ on every $(r+1)$-subset $T$ of an $N$-coordinate set. Let $M_f$ avoid all the selected patterns. For each $(r+2)$-subset $U$, form the graph on its $(r+1)$-subsets, joining two when their selected patterns agree on the common $r$ coordinates. Then $M_f$ is maximum of rank $r$ exactly when every such agreement graph is connected.
hypotheses: Finite binary coordinates, $1\le r<N$, and exactly one selected forbidden pattern on each $(r+1)$-support.
recognition_complexity: For fixed $r$, polynomial in $N$: inspect $\binom{N}{r+2}$ graphs with $r+2$ vertices and compare at most $r$ signs per potential edge.
comments: At $r=N-1$ the single forbidden full word is maximum with no graph checks; at $r=0$ the avoider is a singleton.
